svg.title: Subsets of each language: read, translated, proved
svg.desc: For TypeScript, Go and PostgreSQL, nested regions show the whole language, the subset the parser reads, the subset the translator accepts with a meaning that is trusted and tested, and what is proved.
svg.text: Subsets of each language: what Tolean reads, translates and proves
TypeScript
The language
not read: classes, arrow functions and closures,
async, generics on functions, exceptions,
template literals, imports, regular expressions,
lone surrogates, legacy octal, non-ASCII names
Read by the parser (tested against tsc)
read but not translated: while, break and continue
in loops, return inside a loop, recursion, ==, bit
operators, typeof, in, instanceof, === on objects,
fractional numbers, / and % on number, Math.*,
assigning parameters, fields or const
Translated: meaning trusted, tested
bigint as Int, with / and % by a nonzero literal
(tested against the engine)
number on safe integers, NaN and ±Infinity
(laws tested on Node 22 and 24)
T | null with narrowing, as Option T
interfaces as structures, arrays as List
for … of as List.foldl; local mutation;
push onto an array the function owns
output equals the tsc-based translator's
translation correctness: not proved
(a certificate is planned)
Proved
facts derived from the number laws,
such as eq a a = !isNaN a
each project's claims about its
translated code, by the Lean kernel,
with #audit_claims
these assume the translation and
the number laws are right
Go
The language
not read: generics, channels, go statements,
select, goto, labels, fallthrough, imaginary
numbers, three-index slices, [...]T arrays,
non-ASCII names
Read by the parser (tested against go/parser)
read but not translated: defer, function literals,
type switches and assertions, maps, pointers
(except erased ones), for loops other than range
over a slice, / and %, break inside switch,
effectful calls inside expressions
Translated: meaning trusted, partly tested
structs with zero values, named types, aliases
int and int64 with wrapping (Go Spec: not yet
tested against the Go runtime), bool, string
slices as List, [N]T as Vector
errors.New and fmt.Errorf with %w
interface calls as steps in StateM State
range over slices with break, continue and
return; if, switch, multiple results, methods
erased tracing and timing code
corpus output fixed and compiled in CI
translation correctness: not proved (needs
a Go semantics; none is complete yet)
Proved
wrap64 is the identity on in-range values
each project's claims, for every store
that keeps the interface's contract
with a store on translated SQL: that the
store keeps the contract, too
these assume the translation, the Go Spec
and the compiler are right
PostgreSQL (sqlc queries)
The language
not read: INSERT and DELETE (not yet), ORDER BY,
GROUP BY, LIMIT, DISTINCT, UNION, outer joins,
CASE, IN, BETWEEN, LIKE, JSON operators,
WITH RECURSIVE, $1 parameters
Read by the parser (tested indirectly)
read but not translated: full scans, functions
other than now, LEAST and COALESCE, NULL literals,
operators on nullable values, CHECK and partial
unique on modeled tables, sqlc.narg, an UPDATE
that uses a stale read of its own table
Translated: tested against PostgreSQL 18
schema from migrations: tables, enums, domains,
keys, foreign keys, unique, defaults; equal to
the catalog
SELECT and joins by primary key; UPDATE by key,
with FROM and RETURNING; data-modifying WITH
EXISTS, scalar subqueries, casts, LEAST,
COALESCE, now(); three-valued logic;
bigint overflow errors
every result agrees with the server on
generated scenarios
translation correctness: not proved
(gram.y or a formal SQL semantics planned)
Proved
READ COMMITTED, for updates by key: in every
interleaving, kept properties hold and no
update is lost (model tested on the server)
each project's claims about its queries,
such as that a store keeps a contract
these assume the translation, the Postgres
Spec and Valid are right

g.text: translated: meaning trusted, tested where noted

svg.text: Each ring lists what is in it but not in the ring inside it. The proved ring is about translated code: a proof holds for the program that
runs as far as the rings around it are right.
